CLAUDE.md

Source: CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

What this is

Where To Work is a Shiny web application for systematic conservation planning, built with the golem framework. Because of golem, the app is structured and distributed as an R package (wheretowork) rather than a plain server.R/ui.R Shiny app — run_app() is the entry point, and app.R at the repo root just calls it.

Common commands

Commands below are Makefile targets (run via make <target>); the underlying R calls are shown so they can be run directly in an R console too.

  • Launch the app locally for development: make debug (golem::run_dev() with golem.app.prod = FALSE). make quick-debug sets quick = TRUE in addition, which is read by app_global.R/project-import code to skip loading the full project set for faster iteration.
  • Run the full test suite: make test (devtools::test(), output goes to test.log).
  • Run a single test file from an R console: devtools::test_active_file("tests/testthat/test_new_dataset.R") or testthat::test_file("tests/testthat/test_new_dataset.R").
  • Regenerate man/*.Rd from roxygen comments after changing docs/exported function signatures: make man (devtools::document()). Do this whenever a roxygen block changes — the man/ files are committed and checked by R CMD check.
  • Run R CMD check: make check.
  • Spell-check documentation: make spellcheck.
  • Install the package locally: make install.
  • Regenerate simulated example project data under inst/extdata/projects: make data.
  • Build the pkgdown site: make site (full) or make quicksite (lazy, only changed R/, vignettes/, README.md, NEWS.md, DESCRIPTION, LICENSE.md, _pkgdown.yml).
  • Run via Docker: make demo / make demo-kill (docker-compose), or make image to build and push the naturecons/wheretowork image.

CI (.github/workflows/R-CMD-check-{ubuntu,windows}.yaml) runs rcmdcheck with error_on = "warning" and reports coverage via covr::codecov() on push/PR to main/master/dev and weekly on a schedule. renv (renv.lock) pins dependency versions; CI restores from it with renv::restore().

Architecture

Package/file naming convention (R/)

File name prefixes indicate role, following the golem convention:

  • app_* — top-level app wiring: app_config.R (reads inst/golem-config.yml via get_golem_config()), app_global.R (startup initialization, analogous to Shiny’s global.R), app_server.R (server-side logic, analogous to server.R), app_ui.R (UI, analogous to ui.R).
  • class_* — R6 classes (see below) that model the app’s core domain objects.
  • fct_* — standalone analysis/data functions (project I/O, solving, simulating example data).
  • server_* — chunks of server-side reactive logic, each defined as a quote({...}) block and eval()’d inside app_server (see file header comments for the exact eval(server_x) usage) — this is how the server logic is split across files despite Shiny wanting one server function.
  • ui_* — functions that programmatically build HTML/UI fragments for the front end.
  • widget_* — custom htmlwidgets (JS-backed widgets), each typically split into _ui.R, _server.R, and _html.R/_server.js companions. JS/CSS assets live under inst/htmlwidgets/lib/<widget-name>-<version>/.
  • utils_* — internal helper functions (spatial I/O, raster helpers, color palettes, file validation, Excel export, etc).

DESCRIPTION’s Collate field lists the intended load order (classes before the functions that use them, etc.) — check it if you add a new file, since golem/roxygen relies on #' @include directives plus this ordering.

Domain model (R6 classes)

The app’s state revolves around a fixed set of R6 classes (R/class_*.R), all constructed via a new_*() helper function of the same name (e.g. new_dataset() constructs a Dataset):

  • Dataset — wraps a project’s spatial data (sf/terra::rast()), attribute data (tibble), and boundary data (sparse matrix), each optionally lazy-loaded from a file path (spatial_path, attribute_path, boundary_path) or held "memory"-resident.
  • Theme, Weight, Include, Exclude — the planning inputs a user configures (conservation features/themes to prioritize, weighting layers, must-include/must-exclude constraints). Each has a paired *Results class (ThemeResults, WeightResults, IncludeResults, ExcludeResults) holding computed statistics for a generated solution, and is built from Feature/Variable/Parameter/Statistic building blocks.
  • Solution — a generated prioritization result.
  • SolutionSettings — the current set of theme/weight/include/exclude/parameter settings driving solution generation; exposes getters like get_theme_settings(), get_parameter() used throughout the server_* reactive code.
  • MapManager — manages the Leaflet map’s layers/legends for the currently displayed data.
  • *Legend (CategoricalLegend, ContinuousLegend, ManualLegend, NullLegend) — legend rendering strategies used by MapManager.
  • Provenance, Result, Parameter, Statistic, Variable — supporting value objects.

Project data format

A “project” (what users load/import) is a directory containing a YAML config file plus data files, e.g. inst/extdata/projects/sim_raster/: <name>_data.yaml (theme/weight/include/exclude definitions and metadata), <name>_spatial.tif or .shp (spatial data, raster or vector), <name>_attribute.csv.gz (attribute table), <name>_boundary.csv.gz/.dat.gz (boundary length matrix for spatial clustering). fct_read_project.R/read_project() parses this into the Dataset/Theme/Weight/Include/Exclude objects above; fct_write_project.R is the inverse. The set of bundled example/demo projects lives under inst/extdata/projects/; production deployments point projects: (in inst/golem-config.yml) at an external /projects directory instead (see make prod-data).

Solution generation flow

Triggered from server_generate_new_solution.R: settings and data are pulled off app_data (the app’s central reactive state list) and passed to fct_min_set_result.R / fct_min_shortfall_result.R, which build and solve a prioritizr mixed-integer program (solved via rcbc, or Gurobi if available/licensed). Solving runs as a future (see strategy config: multicore/multisession) so the UI stays responsive and can be cancelled (ipc::stopMulticoreFuture); two solver passes run with different optimality gaps/time limits (solver_gap_1/solver_time_limit_1 for the initial solution, solver_gap_2/solver_time_limit_2 for spatial-clustering refinement) — see inst/golem-config.yml.

Configuration

Runtime configuration is read via get_golem_config(value) (R/app_config.R), which reads inst/golem-config.yml through the config package, keyed by the GOLEM_CONFIG_ACTIVE/ R_CONFIG_ACTIVE env var (defaulting to "default"). Named configs include dev, beginner, advanced, project — these set the app mode (which affects e.g. whether goal limits and mandatory-include settings are enabled), the projects directory, and solver time limits/optimality gaps.
